answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits confirm fabricated work, while limiting how much influence newly bonded identities gain until they complete costly, randomly assigned tasks. Auditors compare signed task logs and outcomes, so copying a profile alone does not create a credible signal. A sable-colored badge or a lagoon-themed name earns no trust; the attacker must lock capital, operate many agents, and risk losing bonds for each detected fake, making a large Sybil swarm expensive to sustain.
